dialogue: Emma: I want to understand the differences between conditional sentences.
أريد أن أفهم الفروق بين الجمل الشرطية.
David: Let's start with a general fact. What happens if you don't water a plant?
لنبدأ بحقيقة عامة. ماذا يحدث إذا لم تسقِ نبتة؟
Emma: If you don't water a plant, it dies.
إذا لم تسقِ نبتة، فإنها تموت.
David: Good. That's the Zero Conditional. Now, what will you do if it rains tomorrow?
جيد. هذا هو الشرط الصفري. والآن، ماذا ستفعلين إذا أمطرت غدًا؟
Emma: If it rains tomorrow, I will stay at home.
إذا أمطرت غدًا، فسأبقى في المنزل.
David: Excellent. That's the First Conditional. What would you do if you won a million dollars?
ممتاز. هذا هو الشرط الأول. ماذا ستفعلين لو ربحت مليون دولار؟
Emma: If I won a million dollars, I would buy a house.
لو ربحت مليون دولار، لاشتريت منزلًا.
David: That's the Second Conditional. Now imagine you didn't study for an exam last week. What would have happened if you had studied?
هذا هو الشرط الثاني. تخيلي أنك لم تدرسي لامتحان الأسبوع الماضي. ماذا كان سيحدث لو كنت قد درست؟
Emma: If I had studied, I would have passed the exam.
لو كنت قد درست، لكنت نجحت في الامتحان.
David: Exactly. That's the Third Conditional. Finally, what would your life be like now if you had studied a different subject?
بالضبط. هذا هو الشرط الثالث. وأخيرًا، كيف كانت حياتك ستكون الآن لو كنت قد درست مادة مختلفة؟
Emma: If I had studied medicine, I would be a doctor now.
لو كنت قد درست الطب، لكنت طبيبة الآن.
David: Perfect! That's a Mixed Conditional.
ممتاز! هذه جملة شرطية مختلطة.
reading: Every day, people make decisions that affect their lives. Some decisions are small, while others can change their future completely.
If people make healthy choices, they usually feel better. For example, if someone exercises regularly and eats well, they often have more energy.
In the future, if students develop good study habits, they will probably achieve better results. However, if they don't manage their time, they may struggle with their responsibilities.
Sometimes people imagine different lives. A person might say, "If I had more free time, I would travel around the world." This is an example of an imaginary situation in the present.
People also think about their past decisions. Someone who failed an important exam might say, "If I had prepared better, I would have passed." This person is imagining a different past.
Other situations connect the past with the present. A woman who did not study medicine might say, "If I had studied medicine, I would be a doctor now."
Finally, some people connect a present characteristic with a past result. Someone who often acts carelessly might say, "If I were more careful, I wouldn't have made that mistake yesterday."
Conditional sentences help us describe facts, future possibilities, imaginary situations, regrets, and the relationship between past and present.
